prompt: Classify a BMI value into a category: below 18.5 is "underweight", below 25 is "normal", below 30 is "overweight", and 30 or above is "obese".
explanation: When ranges are checked in increasing order with an if / else if chain, each branch only needs an upper bound: reaching else if (bmi < 25) already guarantees bmi >= 18.5, because the earlier branch would have caught anything smaller. This makes range classification code short and avoids duplicated compound conditions like bmi >= 18.5 && bmi < 25. The final else catches everything at 30 and above.
hints: Check the smallest range first: if (bmi < 18.5) return "underweight";
In an else if chain each later branch already knows the earlier tests failed, so else if (bmi < 25) alone means 18.5 <= bmi < 25.
Boundary values go up: exactly 18.5 is "normal", exactly 25 is "overweight", exactly 30 is "obese".
